extracted.intended_audience: federally insured credit unions (FICUs), credit union staff, NCUA examiners and attorneys, and members/accountholders seeking to understand share insurance coverage for trust accounts
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register final rule amending 12 CFR part 745 to simplify share insurance coverage for funds held in trust accounts at federally insured credit unions, including merging revocable and irrevocable trust categories, defining beneficiary eligibility, specifying a common coverage calculation, and setting recordkeeping and pass-through requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merger of revocable and irrevocable trust categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Merge the revocable and irrevocable trust categories into one 'trust accounts' category for share insurance purposes, treating funds held in connection with either type of trust under the same coverage rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: reduces confusion and the need for a threshold inquiry into trust form; aligns coverage with substance (trustee holds funds for beneficiaries) rather than legal form. The final rule adopts the proposed changes as described in the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: General calculation of trust coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposited trust funds are insured in an amount up to the SMSIA multiplied by the total number of beneficiaries identified by each grantor, up to a maximum of five beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes a single simplified formula that applies to both revocable and irrevocable trusts (uses the calculation NCUA adopted in 2008 for revocable trusts with five or fewer beneficiaries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation for purposes of insurance limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposited trust funds that pass from the same grantor to beneficiaries are aggregated for the purposes of determining coverage under this section, regardless of whether those funds are held in connection with an informal revocable trust, formal revocable trust, or irrevocable trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example guidance in preamble: funds in living trusts and payable-on-death accounts that pass to the same beneficiaries from the same grantor are aggregated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate insurance coverage from other account categories
rubrics_metrics.description: The share insurance coverage provided for trusts is separate from coverage provided for other funds at the same federally insured credit union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust coverage does not automatically combine with single ownership, joint, or other account categories unless specific rules require aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal allocation presumed for multiple grantors
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise specified in the account records of the federally insured credit union, deposited funds held in connection with a trust established by multiple grantors are presumed to have been owned or funded by the grantors in equal shares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This presumption can be rebutted by account records that specify different allocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible beneficiaries definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiaries include natural persons, as well as charitable organizations and other non-profit entities recognized as such under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only these categories of beneficiaries count toward the beneficiary multiplier used in the coverage calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible beneficiaries definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiaries do not include: (i) the grantor of a trust; or (ii) a person or entity that would only obtain an interest in the deposited funds if one or more named beneficiaries are deceased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contingent beneficiaries who only take if others are deceased are excluded for counting purposes; retained interests of grantors are also excluded (treated as single ownership funds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of future trusts named as beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: If a trust agreement provides that trust funds will pass into one or more new trusts upon the death of the grantor(s) ('future trusts'), the future trust(s) are not treated as beneficiaries; rather, the beneficiaries are the natural persons or organizations that shall receive the trust funds through the future trusts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look through future-trust constructs to the ultimate persons or organizations who will receive funds; do not count the future trust itself as a beneficiary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal trust payable to member's formal trust treated as formal trust
rubrics_metrics.description: If an informal revocable trust designates the account owner's formal trust as its beneficiary, the informal revocable trust account will be treated as if titled in the name of the formal trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures consistent treatment when an informal account points to a formal trust as beneficiary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account-records requirement for informal revocable trusts
rubrics_metrics.description: The beneficiaries of an informal revocable trust must be specifically named in the account records of the federally insured credit union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to name beneficiaries in account records for informal trusts will disqualify the account from being treated as an informal revocable trust for coverage purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account-records requirement for formal revocable trusts
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of a formal trust account must include terminology sufficient to identify the account as a trust account (e.g., 'family trust' or 'living trust'), or must otherwise be identified as a testamentary trust in the account records. If eligible beneficiaries of such formal revocable trust are specifically named in the account records, the NCUA shall presume the continued validity of the named beneficiaries' interest in the trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepts electronic account records (coding) and allows presumption of continued validity where beneficiaries are recorded; but absence of naming means NCUA may need to obtain documentation in a liquidation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocable-trust co-owners who are sole beneficiaries treated as joint funds
rubrics_metrics.description: If the co-owners of an informal or formal revocable trust are the trust's sole beneficiaries, deposited funds held in connection with the trust are treated as joint ownership funds under §745.8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents double-counting: co-owners who are also sole beneficiaries get joint-account treatment rather than trust-account treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee benefit plan deposits exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Deposited funds of employee benefit plans, even if held in connection with a trust, are treated as employee benefit plan funds under §745.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust-account rules do not apply to employee benefit plan funds; such funds follow the employee benefit plan rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption and treatment when no eligible beneficiaries are named
rubrics_metrics.description: In the unlikely event a trust does not name any eligible beneficiaries, the NCUA would treat the funds in the trust account as funds held in a single ownership account. Such funds would be aggregated with any other single ownership funds that the grantor maintains at the same FICU and insured up to the SMSIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the default fallback to prevent unintended separate trust coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Life estate and present-value valuation rules (historical/interpretive guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under current rules referenced in the preamble, a life estate interest is valued at the SMSIA; non-contingent interests may be determined without evaluation of contingencies except those covered by present-worth and life-expectancy tables and IRS rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although final rule adopts simplified beneficiary-count calculation for up to five beneficiaries, the preamble explains when valuation or present-value methods may be relevant for certain types of interests under prior rules or for interests beyond the simplified method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of accounts naming the same beneficiaries
rubrics_metrics.description: All funds that an owner holds in both living trust accounts and payable-on-death accounts, at the same NCUA-insured credit union and naming the same beneficiaries, are aggregated for insurance purposes and insured to the applicable coverage limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage is based on unique beneficiaries per grantor across account types—duplicate beneficiary names across accounts do not multiply coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continued application of revocable-trust coverage upon grantor death (historical practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The pre-existing revocable trust provision that a revocable trust that becomes irrevocable due to death may continue to be insured under the revocable trust rules is noted in the preamble; the NCUA recognized this provision previously to avoid coverage reductions upon death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble discusses this historical rule and its rationale (six-month protection after death, etc.). The final rule's merger must be read in context of these transition/continuity concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership/eligibility requirement for trust coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The longstanding NCUA position remains: for revocable trust accounts, all grantors of the trust must be members of the FICU or otherwise eligible to maintain an insured account; for irrevocable trust accounts, either all grantors or all beneficiaries must be members or otherwise eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule does not alter these longstanding positions but will continue to evaluate commenters' feedback on possible changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of substance over form in insurance determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Share insurance coverage should conform to the substance of the trust arrangement rather than its legal form—i.e., similar economic arrangements should result in similar coverage regardless of legal structuring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as policy principle supporting merger of categories and other simplifications; helps avoid differing coverage solely because of technical trust form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pass-through (IOLTA/escrow) coverage conditional requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Pass-through coverage for lawyers trust accounts and similar escrow accounts will only be available if the recordkeeping requirements of §745.2(c)(1) and the relationship disclosure requirements of §745.2(c)(2) are satisfied; if satisfied, funds attributable to each client and principal will be insured on a pass-through basis in whatever right and capacity the client or principal owns the funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: an IOLTA must be titled as such; insured-credit-union records must indicate the relationship; relationship details must be ascertainable from credit union records or records maintained in good faith by the attorney/escrow agent; NCUA will determine sufficiency in its sole discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCUA discretion on sufficiency of records for pass-through coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The NCUA will determine, in its sole discretion, the sufficiency of the records for an IOLTA or other similar escrow account to establish pass-through coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if minimal records exist, NCUA may require more; sufficiency is not strictly defined and is subject to NCUA judgment during liquidations or examinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Removal of appendix to part 745 and conforming amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule removes the appendix to part 745 and makes conforming amendments throughout part 745 to reflect the merged trust category and other changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural/structural requirement; implementers should update internal procedures and reference materials to align with revised CFR text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates and phased applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule states an overall effective date of December 1, 2026, except for specific amendments to 12 CFR 745.2(c)(2), 745.3, and 745.14, which are effective October 30, 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit unions and other stakeholders must apply earlier-effective provisions as of Oct. 30, 2024, and plan to comply with the remainder by Dec. 1, 2026.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of grantor retained interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds held for a grantor's retained interest in an irrevocable trust are not covered under the trust category and are aggregated with the grantor's other single ownership funds for purposes of applying the share insurance limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retained interests by grantors should be tracked and combined with single ownership accounts for insurance calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on beneficiary multiplier for multiple grantors
rubrics_metrics.description: Coverage is calculated per grantor (e.g., two co-grantors that designate five beneficiaries are insured for up to 2 × 5 × SMSIA), subject to the maximum five-beneficiary cap per grantor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble explicitly notes multiplier effect for multiple grantors; implementers must compute coverage per grantor and aggregate appropriately.
